1. SCOPE: Estimand: mean age of customers who converted (converted ==1) in years, population all customers who converted. The analyst computed mean age of valid converted customers after excluding QA orders, refunded orders, and sentinel -1 ages. Are QA orders and refunded orders part of "customers who converted"? The definition: converted ==1 indicates completed checkout. However, refunded orders have status 'refunded' but still converted ==1. The contract says population: all customers who converted (converted ==1). It does not say to exclude refunded orders. The analyst excluded refunded orders, assuming they are not real conversions. That changes the population. So scope is violated: they excluded some converted customers (refunded). Also excluded QA orders, but QA orders have revenue 999999.99 and converted ==1? The QA orders are not real orders, but they are in data. The contract didn't say to exclude them. However, they are not real customers, but they are rows. The question: "All customers who converted". QA orders are not customers. But they are rows with converted==1. The contract didn't mention QA orders. Excluding them changes denominator. So scope issue.

2. GROUNDING: The numeric claim 45.41 matches printed mean_age_converted_valid = 45.40833. Yes. They also claim number of valid converted customers with non-missing age: 240, which matches printed len(valid_converted_with_age) = 240. Good. They claim number of QA orders: 6 (printed). Refunded converted orders: 21 (printed). So grounded.

3. OVERREACH: No causal claim; just mean. So fine.

4. UNACKNOWLEDGED DATA PROBLEMS: They excluded -1 sentinel values, which is appropriate. They excluded QA orders and refunded orders, but they didn't mention that refunded orders are part of converted population per contract. That's a data problem they ignored: the contract's population includes them. So they ignored that. Also they didn't address that revenue being string but they handled it. No other issues.

5. FALSE PREMISE: Not applicable.

Thus main issue: Scope violation by excluding refunded orders (and possibly QA orders). The contract didn't say to exclude them. So verdict revise, issue: scope mismatch (population definition). Also maybe note that they excluded QA orders which are not real customers but still part of data; but contract didn't specify. So mention scope.
